title: Short Sales - How to Buy & Sell
summary: Comprehensive training on short sales covering what they are, why sellers and buyers participate, the approval process, key departments (loan servicing vs loss mitigation), critical forms, and negotiation strategies. Marty shares real-world examples from the 2008 crash era and current market conditions.

broker_guidance.scenario: Defining a short sale for clients
broker_guidance.guidance: A short sale is when the current fair market value of the property is less than the debt owing against it. The seller cannot sell unless creditors/third parties agree to accept less than what's owed. Third parties may include mortgage lenders, insurers, bankruptcy trustees, and taxing authorities.
broker_guidance.client_language: You owe more on the house than it's currently worth, and we need the bank's permission to sell it for less than you owe.

broker_guidance.scenario: Seller asks why they should do a short sale instead of foreclosure
broker_guidance.guidance: Short sales are easier on credit than foreclosures. Credit recovers faster. The deficiency is typically much lower. Foreclosure can result in the bank coming after the seller for the deficiency plus legal expenses. Short sale sellers usually stay in the home and care for it, unlike foreclosure where sellers may damage or strip the property.
broker_guidance.client_language: A short sale will hurt your credit less than a foreclosure, and you'll likely owe less money afterward. It also keeps you in control of the process longer.

broker_guidance.scenario: Avoiding a short sale when possible
broker_guidance.guidance: Before pursuing a short sale, explore alternatives: negotiate commissions, have buyer pay closing costs (or lender pay via slightly higher rate), loan modification, deed in lieu of foreclosure, or bankruptcy consultation. Do not give legal or tax advice - refer to appropriate professionals.
broker_guidance.client_language: Before we go down the short sale path, let's see if there are other options that might work better for your situation.

broker_guidance.guidance: The loan servicing department handles late payments, notices of default, and foreclosures. They are NOT your advocate. They incentivize reps based on calls per hour, not customer satisfaction. They often lose paperwork. Expect to submit authorization forms multiple times. Many require wet signatures, not digital. You will rarely talk to the same person twice.
broker_guidance.client_language: The bank's servicing department handles a huge volume of calls. We'll need to be patient but persistent, and I'll keep detailed records of every conversation.

broker_guidance.guidance: Loss mitigation protects the lender against losses. They have formulas and stacks of files. They don't care about you or the seller - their job is to minimize losses. Keep a detailed conversation log: name, time, what was discussed, expectations set, promises made, what was requested and provided. This can accelerate the process from 6 months to 60 days. When calling, reference previous conversations to show persistence.
broker_guidance.client_language: The loss mitigation team has one job: minimize the bank's losses. I'll be professional but firm, and I'll document every single conversation to keep things moving.

broker_guidance.scenario: Setting buyer expectations on short sale timeline
broker_guidance.guidance: Short sales can take anywhere from 2 days to over a year. Most currently take 2-4 months. The only guarantee is that something unreasonable will happen. Buyers should continue looking at other properties while waiting. The seller or buyer can cancel up until third party approval or the approval deadline. A foreclosure can still happen even during the short sale process.
broker_guidance.client_language: I have to be honest with you - short sales are unpredictable. The bank can take months to respond, and there's always a curveball. We should keep looking at other homes while we wait.

broker_guidance.scenario: Why buyers get discounts on short sales
broker_guidance.guidance: Buyers typically get 4-6% off market price (sometimes 4-5%). The discount exists because fewer buyers are willing to deal with the uncertainty, timeline, and process. There's tons of regular inventory now, so buyers have options. The short sale addendum gives the seller a 'get out of jail free card' - they can cancel for any reason without waiting.
broker_guidance.client_language: Short sales often sell below market value because many buyers don't want to deal with the uncertainty. If you're patient and flexible, we might get a good deal.

broker_guidance.scenario: Artificially low list prices on short sales
broker_guidance.guidance: Some agents list short sales artificially low to generate multiple offers and get the process started with the bank. Once the bank approves a price, you can update the MLS to show 'bank-approved price' which reduces buyer uncertainty. The goal is to get an offer in to start the bank's approval process, not necessarily to sell at that price.
broker_guidance.client_language: That low list price might be a strategy to get offers in the door and start the bank's review process. The actual approved price could be higher.

broker_guidance.guidance: Mortgage companies often dictate maximum commission amounts. What was 6% (3% each side) might get cut to 5% total. The approval letter will specify the approved commission split. Agents won't know the final commission until the approval comes through. Some agents used to charge other agents upfront fees to handle the short sale process for them.
broker_guidance.client_language: The bank may reduce the commission as part of their approval. We'll know the final amount when we get their approval letter.

broker_guidance.guidance: Key forms: 1) Short Sale Disclosure - educates buyer/seller about the process, 2) Addendum to Listing Agreement - warns seller about financial documentation requirements, 3) Short Sale Addendum to REPC - critical, do NOT accept a REPC without this, 4) Backup Addendum - allows multiple backup offers, 5) Acknowledgment of Third Party Approval - activates contract deadlines once approval is received. All forms are in the MLS and Brokermint.
broker_guidance.client_language: There are several specialized forms for short sales that protect everyone involved. I'll make sure we use every required form.

broker_guidance.guidance: The short sale addendum: sets a short sale approval deadline (contract lapses if not approved by this date), specifies when earnest money is deposited (seller wants it immediately for emotional tie, buyer wants to wait until bank approval), allows backup offers, and gives both parties right to cancel up to approval deadline. Contract deadlines should be SHORTER than normal because everyone should be prepared by the time approval comes.
broker_guidance.client_language: The short sale addendum protects you by setting a deadline for bank approval and giving you the right to walk away if things take too long.

broker_guidance.guidance: If there's a notice of default or foreclosure pending, track it 100% of the time. You can often get the foreclosure forestalled with enough time to close the short sale. Call Marty for help navigating this - it can be done but requires persistence and timing.
broker_guidance.client_language: If there's a foreclosure pending, we need to stay on top of both processes. I have resources to help us manage that timeline.

broker_guidance.guidance: Sellers typically have no money or motivation to do repairs on a short sale. They're not getting proceeds from the sale. While repairs can occasionally happen, buyers should expect to handle repairs themselves or negotiate credits. This is different from a standard sale where seller has incentive to make repairs to close the deal.
broker_guidance.client_language: In a short sale, the seller usually can't afford to make repairs. We should plan on handling any needed repairs ourselves after closing.

steps: Determine if property qualifies as short sale (owe more than worth)
Explore alternatives first: loan modification, deed in lieu, bankruptcy consultation
Have seller contact loan servicing department to start process
Submit required authorization forms (often wet signature required)
Document EVERY conversation in a conversation log
Seller provides financial docs: tax returns, bank statements, pay stubs
List property (may use artificially low price to generate offers)
Submit offer(s) to bank for approval
Use Short Sale Addendum with REPC - never accept without it
Set short approval deadline and shorter-than-normal contract deadlines
Once approved, activate contract deadlines and proceed to closing

objections.objection: Why would I do a short sale instead of just walking away?
objections.response: A short sale is easier on your credit than foreclosure, you'll likely owe less in deficiency, and you stay in control longer. Foreclosure can result in the bank coming after you for the difference plus their legal fees. Your credit recovers faster from a short sale.

objections.objection: The bank won't approve a short sale
objections.response: Banks often prefer short sales because they minimize losses compared to foreclosure. The homeowner usually stays and maintains the property. The key is persistence and proper documentation. I've seen them approved in as little as 2 days and as long as a year.

objections.objection: This is taking too long, I found another house
objections.response: That's exactly why we use the short sale addendum - you CAN walk away and look for other properties while we wait. The contract has an approval deadline, and you can cancel anytime before the bank approves it.

That's normal in a short sale. The seller isn't getting proceeds, so they have no money or motivation for repairs. We can either handle repairs after closing, negotiate a credit, or factor repair costs into our offer price.
